description: Rich-text DISPLAY element (ActionUIRichText add-on) backed by the RichText package. Renders a whole Markdown document (headings, code blocks, quotes, lists, GFM tables, inline styling, links) into one native text view, selectable and copyable as a single unit. macOS/iOS/visionOS. Driven by the element value or the markdown property.

markdown.description: Markdown source to render (seed for the element value). Empty or nil renders an empty document

baseFontSize.description: Base font point size; omit for Dynamic Type body

syntaxHighlighting.description: Color fenced code blocks by language. Default from the RichText theme

widthBehavior.description: fill (default): fills the proposed width, left-aligned - block / document layout. hug: sizes to the content width, wrapping only when it exceeds the proposal (the messaging-bubble idiom; pair with frame.maxWidth to cap how wide it grows)

showFindBar.description: A find bar over this document (default false): Cmd-F opens it, Cmd-G / Shift-Cmd-G step through the matches, Escape closes; its menu toggles case, whole-word and diacritic matching. Matches are painted behind the text without re-laying it out. With showFindBar off, states[search] still highlights

value.description: Current Markdown source; write new Markdown to re-render

states.search.description: Runtime query (setElementState key search): a non-empty String highlights every match and, when showFindBar is on, presents the bar with the term without taking the keyboard focus; an empty string clears. The element seeds the key as a String so any text is accepted (core fixes a state key's type on its first write). Re-delivered on every states change, so a value equal to the last applied one is ignored (the reader can close the bar without it springing back); to re-open with the same term set an empty string and then the term again. The element highlights but does not scroll to the match: that needs a scroller reading RichText's current-match anchor, which ActionUI's ScrollView does not yet
